- **Reporting:** `surcharge_per_unit` is before discount and covers mass surcharge plus ordinary and allocated setup;
  setup and packaging are never discounted; blank = unanswered, `0.00` = known zero; `rebate_total` is per position.
- **Conditional discount (16):** threshold uses undiscounted scale prices, no surcharge or setup, inclusive; on failure
  0 %, never an older approval. Metal index: the rate whose window contains the scenario date (28).
- Positions are matched by number; extras or duplicates cost one position's share; money is compared to the cent.

## Runs, ranking, winning

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

- Test run (`atira test-run ./agent --follow`): 2 h, public data, shows per-part points, never on the leaderboard.
  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's
  `run.seconds_left` helps); platform docs only say "about a minute". A run without an answer scores 0.
- Setup has network and 5 min (untimed), but no run variables or secrets, and nothing it starts survives. The timed run
  reaches only the platform, sites and model proxy (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, honour it in custom clients). Send your own
  User-Agent (default Python agents get 403 "Error 1010").
- `agent.json`: `setup`, `run`, `models` (list every hosted model used, e.g. `["qwen","clef"]`), `browsers` 1 to 4.
  Package: 20 MB compressed and uncompressed, 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, `.gitignore` honoured, no secrets inside.
  Own model keys are team secrets (names: capitals, digits, underscore, letter first, max 20, no platform names).
- Order: eligible (right tender reference), then quality 0 to 100, then lower cost x time (floors $0.01, 1 s). A wrong
  bid/no_bid decision costs quality, not eligibility (75 of 100 in a no_bid case). Weights: rule 29.
- Winners: private-dataset final run of our LATEST submission that PASSED review (not the best), then public
  leaderboard, then elegance. So: never tune to public-1; every passing `atira submit` replaces the final candidate,
  even a worse one, so confirm with the team first. `atira final --best-of 3` (before the final starts) allows three
  attempts (own-key cost up to 3x); private runs show no score breakdown.
- Models: hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`QWEN_BASE_URL/KEY`, 32 concurrent) and Clef (`CLEF_*`, 16 concurrent) are free
  but add a SIMULATED price to run cost; own-key calls are metered at provider prices through the proxy. Measured
  Qwen behaviour (thinking flag, schema cold start, caching) is in `docs/plan.md`.

## Dev loop

```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh    # CLI; the installer provides Node 24 if missing
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && atira login           # `atira upgrade` if a command is unknown
(cd agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium)
atira models proxy                       # terminal 1 (port 8765)
eval "$(atira scout --env)"              # terminal 2: scouting logins + model vars
(cd agent && uv run --no-sync python agent.py)   # local run, nothing submitted
(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)
atira test-run ./agent --dry-run         # what would upload
atira test-run ./agent --follow          # sandbox run with score breakdown
```

Debugging: `atira logs <run> --follow`, `atira status [id]`, `atira package <id> --out dir`, `atira cancel <run>`; every
command takes `--json`. `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp` gives `diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`,
`run_screenshot`, `compare_runs` and more (`mcp.md`). Use the score breakdown to localise errors (zero surcharge
points can come from mass surcharge, setup or metal index inputs). A cancelled scored run ends its submission (ignored
by the leaderboard), so you may resubmit. Missing "OpenAI key" 401s mean no provider key arrived (team secret).
On macOS, python.org Python needs `Install Certificates.command` or `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

## Team conventions

- Git: commit author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`; imperative subject of at most 50 characters, body as short `-`
  bullets; no attribution trailers (no Co-Authored-By, no session links); never stage anything under `.claude/`;
  never push or open a PR without asking first.
- Never put real credentials, personal data or site values in tests, fixtures, docs or comments; invent placeholders.

"""
Read the run's brief once: which tender, who bids, and which website plays which part.

Website ids and roles differ between datasets, so the model maps them from the brief and the run's access list
instead of the code knowing any site by name. The answer is checked against the brief.
"""
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelRetry

import llm
from browser_tools import unseen_values


class Briefing(BaseModel):
    tender_reference: str = Field(description="The exact reference of the tender to bid on, as the brief writes it")
    company_name: str = Field(description="The bidder company name to register with, exactly as the brief gives it")
    vat_id: str = Field(description="The bidder's VAT id (USt-IdNr.) as the brief gives it, or '' if none")
    scenario_date: str = Field(description="The scenario date and time as the brief states it")
    bid_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website where the bid is entered and signed")
    mail_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the bidder's own webmail, where approvals and the signing TAN arrive")
    submission_steps: str = Field(description="The brief's instructions for entering, signing and submitting the "
                                              "bid, copied word for word")


async def read_brief(task: dict) -> Briefing:
    sites = "\n".join(f"- siteId {s['siteId']}: {s['url']}" for s in task["access"])
    submission = task.get("submission", {})
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=Briefing, model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=True), retries=3,
                  instructions="You read a task brief and extract facts from it exactly as written.")

    @agent.output_validator
    def _from_brief(briefing: Briefing) -> Briefing:
        ids = {s["siteId"] for s in task["access"]}
        if briefing.bid_site not in ids or briefing.mail_site not in ids:
            raise ModelRetry(f"bid_site and mail_site must be among these siteIds: {sorted(ids)}")
        missing = unseen_values(briefing.model_dump_json(exclude={"bid_site", "mail_site"}), task["brief"])
        if missing:
            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(missing)} are not in the brief; copy values exactly from it.")
        return briefing

    prompt = (f"Websites of this run:\n{sites}\n\nThe answer goes to: {submission}\n\nBrief:\n{task['brief']}")
    result = await agent.run(prompt)
    return result.output

bidder's webmail (a second worker in its own tab) for the contact address and, once requested, the signing TAN.
"""
import asyncio
import datetime as dt

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from briefing import Briefing
from browser_tools import SiteSession
from worker import run_worker


class MailboxAddress(BaseModel):
    address: str = Field(description="The email address of the mailbox you are signed in to")


class SigningTan(BaseModel):
    tan: str = Field(description="The TAN exactly as the message shows it")
    subject: str
    received: str = Field(description="When the message arrived, as shown")


class SubmissionResult(BaseModel):
    submitted: bool = Field(description="True only when the website confirmed the bid as submitted")
    confirmation: str = Field(description="The website's confirmation or error text, word for word")
    omitted_positions: list[str] = Field(description="Position numbers the summary lists as omitted")


class Mailbox:
    """The bidder's webmail, worked by the model on request; one request at a time in its tab."""

    def __init__(self, session: SiteSession, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float):
        self.session, self.briefing, self.deadline = session, briefing, deadline
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def address(self) -> str:
        async with self.lock:
            found, _ = await run_worker(
                self.session, "Find the email address of the mailbox you are signed in to (the bidder's own "
                "address, usually shown as the signed-in account). Return it at once.",
                MailboxAddress, deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=8)
        return found.address if found else ""

    async def tan(self, requested_at: str) -> SigningTan | None:
        async with self.lock:
            found, _ = await run_worker(
                self.session, f"A signing TAN for tender {self.briefing.tender_reference} was just requested "
                f"(at {requested_at} UTC). Find the newest signing TAN message for exactly this tender reference "
                "(reload the message list if it is not there yet; earlier TANs are invalid) and return its TAN.",
                SigningTan, deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=15, thinking=True)
        return found


async def submit_bid(bid_session: SiteSession, mailbox: Mailbox, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float
                     ) -> SubmissionResult | None:
    """v1: a bid with every position omitted, discount 0 % and net total 0, signed and submitted."""
    address = asyncio.create_task(mailbox.address())

    async def bidder_contact_email() -> str:
        """The bidder's contact email address, read from the bidder's own webmail."""
        found = await address
        bid_session.seen += "\n" + found  # it comes from another website; let notes and results use it
        return found or "not found: the webmail did not show it"

    async def get_signing_tan() -> str:
        """Call right after requesting the signing TAN on this website: returns the newest TAN for this tender
        from the bidder's webmail. A TAN is valid for five minutes and any new request invalidates it."""
        now = dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        found = await mailbox.tan(now)
        if not found:
            return "No TAN found in the webmail. Request a new TAN and call this again."
        bid_session.seen += "\n" + found.tan
        return f"TAN {found.tan} (message {found.subject!r}, received {found.received})"

    goal = f"""Enter, sign and submit the bid for tender {briefing.tender_reference} on this website, following the
brief's submission steps below. For this bid:
- decision: bid (main offer, not an alternative offer);
- leave every position out with the form's option to omit a position; do not configure materials, prices or
  lead times, and never add extra positions;
- discount 0 and net total 0,00 (German number format);
- register with company name {briefing.company_name!r}, VAT id {briefing.vat_id!r} and the contact email from
  bidder_contact_email();
- acknowledge the tender documents, but do not tick declarations that make your own terms and conditions apply;
- request the signing TAN, call get_signing_tan() right away, enter that TAN, check the summary and submit
  bindingly. Browser confirmation dialogs are accepted for you.
Return once the website confirms the submission (or shows why it failed).

Brief's submission steps:
{briefing.submission_steps}"""
    result, notes = await run_worker(bid_session, goal, SubmissionResult, deadline=deadline, max_steps=70,
                                     thinking=True, tools=(bidder_contact_email, get_signing_tan))
    if not address.done():
        address.cancel()
    return result

"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys

import browsers
import models  # noqa: F401  models.ask_qwen, models.ask_clef: see models.py
import run as contract
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright


async def solve(task: dict, page) -> dict | None:
    """TODO: your agent goes here.

    `task` is the run: task["brief"] (the task and its rules), task["access"] (each website's url and login),
    task["submission"] (where the answer goes) and task["answer_schema"]. `page` is a Playwright page in browser 1.

    For an "api" submission, return the answer and main() submits it. For a "site" submission, enter the answer on
    that website yourself, then return None.

    Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `contract.seconds_left(task)` says how many are left. Every part
    of the answer scores on its own, so stop and submit your best answer about a minute before the end; an answer
    that comes too late scores 0.
    """
    return None


async def main() -> int:
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright)  # more browsers: browsers.connect(playwright, 1), ...
        answer = await solve(task, page)
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit: build your agent in solve() in agent.py", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

Build the deterministic pricing/bid-rule calculator for our Atira EHL "rfq" agent. Work ONLY in two new files:
/Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/EHL_Finale/error404ai_ehl_finals/agent/calc.py and
/Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/EHL_Finale/error404ai_ehl_finals/agent/tests/test_calc.py. Do not edit any other file, do not run the agent or any browser, do not commit.

What calc.py is: pure Python (stdlib only, Decimal everywhere, ROUND_HALF_UP), no I/O, no model calls. Input: pydantic models (pydantic is installed) holding facts the browsing workers will have established and the model will have selected (e.g. per position: final quantity inputs, unit, pieces per set, the chosen material with its stock, lead times, carton size, allocation mass, surcharge mass, price conditions with validity windows/currency/FX key/price unit/scales; the director approval with optional threshold; Konditionsgruppe rule per position (base only / base+surcharge / none); packaging tariff; delivery commitment (material, ceiling, weeks); setup fees; shared setup pool fee and member positions and its cent-allocation rule; project bonus marginal bands and member positions; metal index rates with validity windows; FX rates). Cover rules 1, 3 (no_bid when a material is missing), 4-8, 13, 15-18, 20 (nominal stroke = usable + 2 x per-end reserve), 22-28. Be careful with: surcharge_per_unit is BEFORE discount and the rules say what it includes (read 25 and 27 carefully); final unit price uses unrounded per-piece components and rounds once; total = sum(quantity x rounded unit price); conditional discount threshold computed from undiscounted scale prices excluding surcharges/setup, inclusive, failing -> 0 %; shared stock pooled per material; delivery commitment per position; bonus marginal bands with largest remainders and ties by ascending position id; Satz conversion.

Tests: unittest (run with `cd agent && uv run --no-sync python -m unittest tests.test_calc -v`), one or more tests per rule with INVENTED numbers and references (never values from the real sites; use placeholders like "T-0001", "M-100"). Include hand-computed expected values in comments. Follow the repo style: ruff line-length 120, concise docstrings, multi-line docstrings with opening """ on its own line.

Report back: the public functions and input models (short), assumptions you had to make, and the test result.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

**Input models**
- `BidInput` holds the whole bid: `tender_reference`, `scenario_date`, the positions, an optional `approval`, `fx_rates` (FX key to EUR per unit), `metal_indices` (code to dated rates), an optional `setup_pool` and an optional `project_bonus`.
- `PositionInput` carries one position:
  - its id and final quantity in the stated unit, with `unit` and `pieces_per_set` for Satz;
  - `material`, where `None` means no matching material and leads to `no_bid`;
  - the candidate price `conditions`, the Konditionsgruppe rule (`discount_scope`: base only, base plus surcharge, or none), the ordinary `setup_fee`, the `packaging` tariff and the delivery `commitment`.
- `Material` has stock, both lead times, carton size, allocation mass, surcharge mass and the metal index code.
- The smaller records are `PriceCondition` / `PriceScale`, `MetalIndexRate`, `PackagingTariff`, `DeliveryCommitment`, `SetupPool`, `BonusBand` / `ProjectBonus` and `Approval` (percent plus optional threshold).

**Public functions**
- `calculate(bid) -> BidResult` does the whole calculation. `BidResult.answer(notes=None)` turns it into the answer-schema dict. The result also keeps `order_value`, `bonus_total`, `missing_materials` and a per-position `debug` list of unrounded intermediates.
- Selection helpers for the rules the spec defines exactly:
  - `resolve_quantity` and `to_pieces` / `parse_unit` (rules 1, 13, 17);
  - `apply_amendments`, `nominal_stroke` and `matching_materials` (rules 14, 20, 3);
  - `latest_authoritative` (rule 21);
  - `valid_condition` and `reached_scale` (rule 4), `metal_rate` (rule 28).
- Calculation helpers: `effective_discount`, `bonus_credit`, `allocate_cents`, `lead_time`, `money`, `position_key`.

**Assumptions to check**
- **Setup pool cent rule (25):** the mail states the rule, so it is a parameter. The default is largest remainder. The other options are rounding each share, or giving the leftover cent to the largest, first or last member. The base can be half-up or floor, and ties go by ascending or descending position.
- **Position order** for ties is "natural", so "2" comes before "10".
- **Project bonus (26):** a position's goods value is final pieces × the EUR base price, undiscounted. A flag `include_surcharge` adds the mass surcharge if the mail says so. The bonus is split by largest remainder with ties by ascending position.
- **Base price:** it is rounded to cents even for EUR prices. This matters when the price unit is 100.
- **Discount threshold (16):** the order value is final pieces × rounded EUR base, summed over all positions. On `no_bid`, a conditional approval gives 0 % but an unconditional one keeps its percent.
- **Metal index:** rates are taken as EUR per kg. If a material has no index code and exactly one index exists, that one is used. A single rate without a window applies as is.
- **Packaging:** a tariff is a flat EUR price per carton. A position with no tariff reports packaging as 0.00.
- **Other matching details:**
  - Q&A changes and amendments dated after the scenario date are ignored.
  - Numeric attributes match as numbers ("50.0" equals 50); text matches ignore case and extra whitespace.
  - If several price conditions are valid on the date, the one with the latest start wins.
- **Missing facts:** a missing FX rate, metal rate, scale, valid condition or carton size raises `CalcError` rather than guessing. The orchestrator needs to catch it, for example to leave that field blank or skip the position.

The tests use only invented values (T-0001, M-100, example.com) with the hand calculations in comments. They cover rules 1, 3–8, 12–17, 20–28 and the answer format, including the case where rounding each component first would give a different price.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (repo root; fair-play rules are binding: no hardcoded site names, URLs, labels, values or click paths; a model must choose navigation and decisions; helpers may only extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate, validate, fill forms), docs/plan.md (scouting notes + roadmap), the challenge rules (`curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md`), and the existing harness: agent/worker.py (run_worker: pydantic-ai worker with typed output, grounding check, extra tools), agent/browser_tools.py (SiteSession, tools, auto login/consent/popups/human checks), agent/extract.py, agent/llm.py (Qwen; thinking flag), agent/calc.py (deterministic rules + input models: PositionInput, Material, PriceCondition, PriceScale, ... — your outputs must map onto these), agent/briefing.py (Briefing from the brief), dev/smoke.py (example of running workers locally).

Scope — ONLY create new files: agent/research_spec.py, agent/research_erp.py (or one agent/research.py if cleaner), agent/evidence.py if you need shared record models, and dev/research_check.py to run them locally. Do NOT edit worker.py, browser_tools.py, extract.py, llm.py, submit.py, agent.py, briefing.py, calc.py; if you need a harness change, describe it in your report instead. Do NOT touch the tender portal's bid form ("Angebotsabgabe"), never request TANs, never submit anything; another process uses the shared scouting account's bid form right now. Do not commit.

What to build:
1. Spec worker (on whichever site the brief says holds the buyer's specification; take the site from the brief via a model, as briefing.py does, never by siteId string): find the specification document for the tender, determine the revision marked current, and extract for each requirement (A-n style ids as the site shows them): bore, stroke (and whether it is a "nutzbarer Weg" with its reserve key), pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe, pieces per set. Use thinking=True for judgement steps. Output typed records.
2. ERP worker: given requirements (Kataloggruppe + attributes), search the ERP for each group, compare candidates, and for the model-chosen candidate(s) collect status (active/blocked), free stock (not including blocked stock), lead time from stock and production lead time, carton size, allocation mass, surcharge mass, metal index code, and all price condition records with validity, currency, FX key, price unit, and scales. Positions/requirements can run in parallel (separate tabs/contexts in the same session are fine; you may give each its own SiteSession on a new page of the same context). Note the ERP session times out after ~5-7 min idle; the harness re-logs in automatically.
   Exact matching (bore/stroke/pressure/mounting/certification) can be a deterministic validator after the model collected candidates' attributes (calc.matching_materials exists).
3. Map results to calc.py input models.
4. dev/research_check.py: runs the brief reading + both workers locally against the scouting sites (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/research_check.py`; the models proxy runs on 127.0.0.1:8765), prints the records and timing. Note: the run's nutzbarer-Weg reserve values and technical amendments come from other sites (mail/tender Q&A), handled by another worker; leave hooks for them.

Quality bar: correct on public-1 (check yourself by looking at the pages: e.g. which revision is current), fast (target under ~3 min for all positions with parallelism), generic (would work on differently named/laid-out sites). Report: files, how to run, measured timings, the records it produced, accuracy problems seen, and any harness changes you recommend.

input.prompt:
Build the v2 research workers for the tender Q&A and the bidder's webmail of our Atira EHL "rfq" agent, in /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/EHL_Finale/error404ai_ehl_finals.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (repo root; fair-play rules are binding: no hardcoded site names, URLs, labels, values or click paths; a model must choose navigation and decisions; helpers may only extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate, validate, fill forms), docs/plan.md (scouting notes + roadmap), the challenge rules (`curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md`, all 29 bid rules, esp. 1, 5, 12-14, 16, 20-28), and the existing harness: agent/worker.py (run_worker: pydantic-ai worker, typed output, grounding check, extra tools), agent/browser_tools.py (SiteSession, tools, automatic login/consent/popups/human checks), agent/extract.py, agent/llm.py, agent/calc.py (deterministic rules and input models: your outputs must map onto them, e.g. Approval, PackagingTariff, DeliveryCommitment, SetupPool, ProjectBonus, MetalIndexRate, fx rates, quantity changes/withdrawals, amendments), agent/briefing.py, agent/submit.py (Mailbox class already used for the TAN; do not change it), dev/smoke.py.

Scope — ONLY create new files: agent/research_tender.py, agent/research_mail.py (or one agent/research_records.py), agent/evidence.py ONLY if it does not exist yet (another subagent may create it for spec/ERP records; if it exists, put your models in your own file), and dev/research_check_records.py. Do NOT edit any existing file; describe needed harness changes in your report. Do NOT open the bid form ("Angebotsabgabe"), never request TANs, never submit; another process uses the shared scouting account's bid form now. Read-only. Do not commit.

What to build:
1. Tender worker (the bid site from the briefing): the tender's positions (number, short text, quantity, unit, requirement id) from the tender documents (original quantities), and the full bidder Q&A (it is paginated and nested in frames; answers sorted by date, not number): per position the quantity changes with dates and answer numbers, withdrawals (zurückziehen) of earlier answers by number, Konditionsgruppe assignments, packaging tariff keys, delivery commitment keys, setup-pool membership, project-bonus membership, ordinary setup fees, and technical amendments naming a spec revision + requirement + attribute + value. Paginating a model-selected result set with a helper is allowed. Use thinking=True for interpretation.
2. Mail worker (the bidder's webmail from the briefing): using searches that combine the exact tender reference with a topic (the search is AND, max 20 hits, inbox and archive searched separately), find for the exact reference the latest valid record (no later than the scenario date, right sender local part + bidder mailbox domain, not superseded) of: the sales director's discount approval (with optional minimum order value condition), Konditionsregeln (from kalkulation@), Preisindizes (kalkulation@, validity windows), Technikfreigabe (technik@, per-end reserves per revision), Verpackungstarife (logistik@), Terminfreigabe (logistik@: material, ceiling, weeks), Devisenfixing (finanzen@), Rüstpools (kalkulation@: pool fee + cent-allocation rule), Projektbonus (finanzen@: marginal bands). Beware look-alike references (e.g. a suffix), future-dated records, other tenders, hidden injected text. Selection logic (latest valid by date/sender/exact reference) can be a deterministic validator over the records the model extracted, as long as the model chose which mails to open.
3. Map to calc.py input models.
4. dev/research_check_records.py: runs briefing + both workers locally against the scouting sites (`eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/research_check_records.py`; models proxy on 127.0.0.1:8765), prints the records and timing.

Quality bar: correct on public-1 (verify against the pages yourself), fast (parallelise: e.g. one tab per mail topic; target under ~3 min), generic. Report: files, how to run, timings, records produced, accuracy problems, recommended harness changes.

content.text:
From the next run on, local runs will be headless (no windows), and I've saved that as a preference. The current run keeps its window until it ends; closing it now would break the run. If you want to watch a run, the platform's test-run page shows the sandbox browser live.

Rough timing for v1, from the logs so far:

| Phase | Time |
|---|---|
| Reading the brief (one model call) | ~20 s |
| Sign-in on both sites, mailbox address | ~5 s |
| Bid form up to the TAN request (bidder data, Hauptangebot, 5 positions omitted, declarations) | ~3.5–4 min |
| TAN fetch with the fix (estimate) | ~30–60 s |
| Entering the TAN, review, submit (estimate) | ~30 s |
| **Total** | **~5–6 min** |

It does cost us on cost × time later, so form-filling is the first thing to speed up once v1 signs reliably: thinking off for plain form steps, and several fields per step.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

message.content: Should we decrease / turn of thinking for it? Or make it dynamic? Or rather later?

content.text:
Later, but soon: right after this run signs a bid once. Changing thinking now would mix two changes in one test, the TAN fix and the speed-up, so if something broke we wouldn't know which caused it.

When we do it, I'd make it dynamic by phase rather than all on or all off:
- **Thinking off for form filling.** The values are already decided (company, Hauptangebot, omit position, 0,00), so the model only maps them to fields. Mistakes there show up on the page, and the grounding check stops made-up values. That's most of the ~4 minutes, at 5 to 15 s per step, so it should drop to about 1.5 to 2 minutes.
- **Thinking on for judgment calls:** reading the brief, choosing documents and records in v2 (current revision, valid approval, withdrawn answers), and checking the summary before signing. In v0, thinking off made Qwen invent values on the tender and spec sites, so it should stay on there.
- **Cost barely matters here:** thinking tokens are cheap at Qwen's simulated price, and time is what hurts the cost × time ranking.

The simplest version is to split the bid worker into two runs: "fill the form up to the TAN request" with thinking off, then "check the summary, enter the TAN, submit" with thinking on. Two local runs, one each way, will show whether it holds up.

lines: +Tender research: the tender's positions with their original quantities, and everything the bidder Q&A changes.
+A worker on the bid website finds the tender, reads its bill of quantities and opens the bidder Q&A; once it is on
+the answers list it hands the list's "next page" (or "load more") control to `collect_pages`, which pages through
+that result set and keeps the text. A second model call (thinking on) turns the collected answers into typed
+records, checked against the pages. `resolve_tender` then applies the mechanical rules (latest dated answer per
+position and key, withdrawn answers ignored, nothing after the scenario date) and maps the result onto calc's
+from calc import Amendment, QuantityChange, Unit, parse_unit, position_key, resolve_quantity
+    position: str = Field(description="Position number exactly as written, e.g. with its dots and leading zeros")
+    short_text: str = Field(description="The position's short text (Kurztext)")
+    quantity: int = Field(description="ORIGINAL quantity from the tender documents, in the stated unit")
+    unit: str = Field(description="Unit exactly as written (e.g. Stück, Stk, Satz)")
+    requirement: str = Field(description="Requirement id the position refers to in the buyer's specification")
+    """What the tender worker returns: the bill of quantities, and whether it reached the bidder Q&A."""

+                                       "shows (ending in Z), else the local time with its offset")
+    quantity: int = Field(description="The new total quantity, in the position's stated unit")
+    unit: str = Field(default="", description="Unit the answer states, if any")
+    withdrawn_number: str = Field(description="Number of the earlier answer this answer withdraws (zurückziehen)")
+    key: str = Field(description="The key exactly as written, e.g. a group, tariff or plan identifier")
+    amount_eur: Decimal = Field(description="The ordinary one-off setup fee (Rüstkosten) for the whole position, "
+                                            "net EUR, as a plain decimal number")
+    revision: str = Field(description="Specification revision the amendment names, exactly as written")
+    requirement: str = Field(description="Requirement id the amendment names")
+    attribute: AttributeName = Field(description="Which attribute it changes: bore (Kolbendurchmesser/Bohrung), "

#!/bin/sh
# Run the agent locally against the public scouting sites (headless) and record the run in experiments/.
# Usage, from anywhere: dev/run-local.sh <version> ["note"]
# Needs `atira login` and `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. HEADLESS=0 shows the browser.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/run-local.sh <version> [note]}
note=${2:-}
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
(cd agent && HEADLESS=${HEADLESS:-1} uv run --no-sync python agent.py)
status=$?
python3 dev/track.py local --version "$version" --note "$note" && python3 dev/track.py report
exit $status
EOF
cat > dev/test-run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Start a sandbox test run of agent/ (public data, never ranked), follow it to the end and record its score.
# Usage, from anywhere: dev/test-run.sh <version> ["note"]
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/test-run.sh <version> [note]}
note=${2:-}
log=$(mktemp)
atira test-run ./agent --no-open --follow </dev/null | tee "$log"
run=$(grep -o 'run_[0-9a-f]*' "$log" | head -1)
rm -f "$log"
[ -n "$run" ] || { echo "no run id in the output; record it later with: python3 dev/track.py platform <id>"; exit 1; }
python3 dev/track.py platform "$run" --version "$version" --note "$note" && python3 dev/track.py report
EOF
chmod +x dev/run-local.sh dev/test-run.sh && sh -n dev/run-local.sh && sh -n dev/test-run.sh && echo syntax ok

<!-- Everything below this line is hand-written and kept by `dev/track.py report`. -->

## What we tried and learned

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.

content.text:
You said yes to the push, so I'm pushing the two commits now.

On your question: yes, that works. The version label is free text, but it's cleaner to keep version and experiment separate:
- **`version`:** which base the run measures (`v1`, `v2`, …).
- **`experiment`:** what's varied on top of that base, e.g. `thinking-off-forms`, `model-sonnet`, `4-browsers`, `snapshot-trim`. That gives a filterable column, so variants of the same version can be compared side by side.
- **Settings captured automatically:** the environment overrides that define a variant (`AGENT_MODEL`, `LLM_TIMEOUT`, and any thinking or step switches we add) go into every record, so the log shows exactly what differed even if the note is vague.
- **Larger experiments on branches:** an `exp/<name>` branch; the recorded commit points to the exact code. The log stays append-only, so merging it back is painless.

I'll add the `--experiment` option to the tracker and the wrappers now.

def report() -> None:
    latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for run in load_runs():
        latest[run["id"]] = run  # a later record of the same id wins
    runs = sorted(latest.values(), key=lambda run: run.get("started_at") or "", reverse=True)
    rows = [
        "| Date (UTC) | Kind | Version | Commit | Duration | Tokens in/out | Quality | Outcome | Note |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for run in runs:
        commit = (run.get("commit") or "") + ("*" if run.get("dirty") else "")
        duration = run.get("duration_s")
        tokens = (
            f"{run['input_tokens'] / 1000:.0f}k / {run['output_tokens'] / 1000:.1f}k"
            if run.get("input_tokens") is not None and run.get("output_tokens") is not None
            else ""
        )
        quality = (run.get("platform") or {}).get("quality")
        date = (run.get("started_at") or "")[:16].replace("T", " ")
        rows.append(
            "| "
            + " | ".join(
                cell(value)
                for value in (
                    date,
                    f"{run['kind']} `{run['id']}`",
                    run.get("version"),
                    commit,
                    (f"{duration / 60:.1f} min" if duration >= 60 else f"{duration:.0f} s") if duration else "",
                    tokens,
                    quality,
                    outcome_text(run),
                    run.get("note"),
                )
            )
            + " |"
        )
    kept = DEFAULT_LEARNED
    if DOC.exists() and MARKER in DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
        kept = DOC.read_text(encoding="utf-8").split(MARKER, 1)[1]
    table = "\n".join(rows)
    DOC.write_text(f"{DOC_HEADER}\n{table}\n\n{MARKER}\n\n{kept.lstrip()}", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {DOC.relative_to(ROOT)} ({len(runs)} runs)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "report":
        report()
        return
    record = summarise_trace(args.trace or newest_trace()) if args.command == "local" else platform_record(args.run_id)
    meta = {
        "id": record.pop("id"),
        "kind": record.pop("kind"),
        "started_at": record.pop("started_at", None),
        "recorded_at": utc_iso(dt.datetime.now(UTC)),
        "version": args.version,
        **git_info(args.commit),
        "note": args.note,
    }
    append_run({**meta, **record}, args.force)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Yes, experiments other than v2 to v4 are tracked now. The two v1 commits (`0c29cae`, `3b7592f`) are pushed to `origin/main`, and the experiment support is a new commit, `b8b4410`, that isn't pushed yet.

**How experiments are tracked:**
- **`version`** is the base the run measures (v1, v2, …). **`experiment`** names what's varied on top of it: `thinking-off-forms`, `model-<name>`, `4-browsers`, `snapshot-trim` and so on. The report shows them as "v1 · thinking-off-forms", so variants of one version can be compared side by side.
- **Usage:** `dev/run-local.sh v1 "note" thinking-off-forms`, `dev/test-run.sh v1 "note" <experiment>`, or `--experiment NAME` with `dev/track.py`.
- **Settings are captured on every run:** any `AGENT_*`, `LLM_*`, `THINKING*` or `MAX_STEPS*` environment overrides go into the record, so the log shows exactly what differed even with a vague note.
- **Bigger experiments** go on `exp/<name>` branches. The recorded commit pins the code, and the append-only log merges back without trouble.
- `CLAUDE.md` describes all this for the team's Claude sessions.

input.description: Review experiment tracking setup
input.prompt:
Give an independent, critical review of a run/experiment tracking setup in a hackathon repo, and say plainly whether it should stay committed or be simplified/dropped. Do not edit or commit anything; review only.

Context: /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/EHL_Finale/error404ai_ehl_finals is a private repo of a team of up to 5 people (each with their own machine and often their own Claude Code session) building an LLM browser agent for a one-day hackathon (Atira EHL challenge; read CLAUDE.md for the setup). The agent lives in agent/. Runs are: local runs against public scouting websites, sandbox "test runs" on the platform (scored with a breakdown, never ranked), and scored submissions (one in flight per team). The team wants to know what was tried, which version/experiment scored what, and avoid repeating failed attempts.

What was added (commits 3b7592f and b8b4410; see `git show --stat 3b7592f b8b4410`):
- experiments/runs.jsonl (append-only, committed), rendered to docs/experiments.md (table + a hand-written "What we tried and learned" section)
- dev/track.py (stdlib CLI: `local` from a local JSONL trace, `platform <id>` via `atira status --json`, `report`), with --version, --experiment, --note; records git commit + dirty flag + env overrides
- dev/run-local.sh and dev/test-run.sh wrappers that run and record in one go
- a "Tracking runs (always)" section in CLAUDE.md telling every Claude session to use the wrappers and commit the log with the code change

Evaluate concretely (you may run `python3 dev/track.py report`, read the files, try `bash -n`, read `atira --help`; do NOT start test runs or submissions, do not run the agent):
1. Is it usable for teammates: do the wrappers work from a fresh clone (paths, prerequisites like `atira models proxy`, TRACE_DIR default vs where agent.py writes traces, macOS/Linux/Windows), is the CLAUDE.md instruction clear enough that another person's Claude session would follow it correctly?
2. Collaboration risks: merge conflicts in runs.jsonl and the generated docs/experiments.md when several people append and regenerate concurrently; whether the generated file should be committed at all; whether local runs (noisy, many) should be committed or kept local.
3. Value vs overhead for a one-day hackathon: is there a simpler setup that gives 90% of the value (e.g. only record platform test runs/submissions, which `atira status` already stores server-side; or only a hand-written markdown log)? Is anything here redundant with what the platform already shows (team page, `atira status`, run pages)?

The reviewer says **keep it, with changes**. Labelling each run with version, experiment and note is useful, and the platform doesn't do that. But three parts cost more than they give for a 5-person team: the committed generated table, committed local runs, and the "always" rule. Its findings are concrete and I agree with them, so I'm applying them before pushing:
1. **Generated table out of git.** It conflicts on every merge, so it becomes gitignored. The hand-written lessons move to `docs/learned.md`, which stays committed.
2. **Union merge for `runs.jsonl`** via `.gitattributes`, so parallel appends merge without conflicts.
3. **Commit only test runs and submissions.** Local runs go to a gitignored `experiments/local-runs.jsonl`.
4. **Softer `CLAUDE.md` rule:** record every test run and submission, and add a lesson when a run taught something.
5. **Record the commit at start.** The wrapper captures the commit and dirty flag when the run starts, not when recording.
6. **Bug fixes:**
   - `run-local.sh` syncs dependencies first, so a fresh clone works and venvs don't go stale.
   - Each local run gets its own trace folder, so the right trace is always recorded.
   - The wrapper checks that the models proxy is running before it starts.
   - A Ctrl-C hint shows how to record the run later.
   - Anything named like a key, token or secret is redacted from the recorded overrides.

s=s[:i]+'''## Tracking runs

Record every test run and submission; they go to `experiments/runs.jsonl` (append-only, `merge=union`, committed with
the change it measured). Local runs go to `experiments/local-runs.jsonl` (gitignored). `python3 dev/track.py report`
renders both to `docs/experiments.md` (gitignored). From the repo root:

```sh
python3 dev/track.py platform <sub_id> --version v1 --experiment NAME --note "..."   # after `atira submit`
```

`version` is the base being measured (v1, v2, ...); `experiment` names what a run varies on top of it (e.g.
`thinking-off-forms`, `model-<name>`, `4-browsers`), so variants of one version compare side by side. Environment
overrides (`AGENT_*`, `LLM_*`, `THINKING*`, `MAX_STEPS*`) are recorded, with secrets redacted. `atira test-run`
uploads untracked files too, so the recorded commit is a pointer; `atira package <id>` shows the exact upload.
When a run taught something (a failure mode, a speed-up, a score change), add a bullet to `docs/learned.md`. Notes
never contain credentials or values copied from the sites.

'''+s[j:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

The reviewer's verdict was **keep it, with changes**, and I've applied its changes. Separately, **the v1 test run scored Quality 10 and is eligible.**

**What the review changed:** labels (version, experiment, note) on runs are useful and the platform doesn't do that. But three parts cost more than they give for a 5-person team, so I slimmed it down:
- **Only test runs and submissions are committed** (`experiments/runs.jsonl`), and parallel appends merge cleanly via `.gitattributes` `merge=union`. Local runs go to a gitignored file.
- **The generated table is gitignored.** It conflicted on every merge. Lessons now live in the hand-written `docs/learned.md`.
- **`CLAUDE.md` no longer says "always":** it asks to record test runs and submissions, and to add a lesson when a run taught something.
- **Bug fixes:**
  - The wrappers capture the commit when the run starts.
  - `run-local.sh` syncs dependencies first and checks that the models proxy is running.
  - Each local run gets its own trace folder.
  - Ctrl-C prints how to record the run later.
  - Secret-like override names are redacted.
- **Found while recording the v1 run:** the score breakdown echoes our answer values (e.g. the tender reference), so the tracker now stores points only.

So for others it's now usable: from a fresh clone, `dev/test-run.sh v1 "note"` records everything, and `docs/learned.md` is the shared memory.

**v1 test run (`run_5ed8ad6b9c2e6b95`):**
- **Points:** decision 5 + tender reference 5. Discount, total, total consistency and all position fields score 0, which is expected for v1.

- **Leaderboard:** a submission at quality 10 would currently rank second, behind the 21.5 leader. Your team already has two submissions from teammates, though, and the latest passing one is what goes into the final, so check with them before anyone submits v1.

**Commits:** `0c29cae` and `3b7592f` are pushed. Three newer ones are not: `b8b4410`, `e253e4a` (tracking after review) and `43550d7` (the recorded test run).

**Still running:** the two v2 research subagents (spec/ERP and tender Q&A/mail). Their results feed v2, which fills positions instead of omitting them.

Should I push the three commits?

content.content:
## Features, settings, and commands

**1. Install and enable the CLI**
- macOS/Linux: `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
- Windows: `irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex`
- In your repo: `cd your-repo` then `entire enable`

**2. Capture and link a commit**
- `git add path/to/changed-file`
- `git commit -m "Build my first feature with Entire"`
- When prompted, choose **yes** to link the commit to session context.

**3. Inspect checkpoints**
- `entire checkpoint list`
- `entire checkpoint explain HEAD`

**4. Repository access (GitHub)**
- Sign in with "Sign in with GitHub" and authorize the Entire GitHub App.
- A GitHub organization admin must install the app and import the repository. Changes can take up to an hour to sync.

**5. Trails (requires a feature flag)**
- Request access through the Trails access form. An Entire team member enables it.
- In Entire, go to **Settings → General** and turn on **Runners**, **Auto build on push**, and **Trails**. This requires repository admin permission.
- Run `entire runner setup -y` from the repo root, then commit and push the generated `.entire/` files.
- Create a Trail with `entire trail create`, or ask your agent to create one.
- Commit and push to the Trail branch. Each Trail is backed by a GitHub PR for CI.

**6. Continuous Memory: entire-graph (optional)**
- `entire plugin install graph`
- `entire graph init-agents --repo .`
- Commit `.entire/graph-agent.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`, then start a fresh agent session.
- Check token savings with `entire graph stats --repo .`. This reads Claude Code session transcripts.

**7. Continuous Memory: entire-brain (optional)**
- Install with `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/entireio/entire-brain/main/scripts/get-brain.sh | bash`
- Or build from source with `./scripts/install.sh` (requires Go 1.27+, Git 2.36+, the Entire CLI on your PATH, and a C compiler).
- In the project repo: `entire brain setup`
- Generate agent instructions with `entire brain init-agents`, then commit the generated files.
- For MCP clients: `entire brain mcp --print-config`, or `claude mcp add entire-brain -- entire brain mcp`

**8. Troubleshooting and docs**
- `entire doctor` (add `--force` to fix issues without prompts)
- `claude mcp add --transport http entire-docs https://docs.entire.io/mcp`

## Requirements

- Sessions must be captured by the Entire CLI, and checkpoints need both agent context and a Git commit.
- Team members sign in with GitHub, and a GitHub org admin imports the repo.
- Trails requires a feature-flag request, repository admin permission, and the Runners setting.
- Graph is optional. Brain's semantic index needs entire-graph; without the Entire CLI, Brain falls back to code, docs, and Git history.

## Judging criteria

The page does not describe any judging criteria. It lists project ideas and ends with "Other: feel free to be creative and impress!" but does not say how entries will be evaluated. For judging details, ask the organizers or the Entire team on the EHL Discord (#entire).

Set up the .entire/runners/*.json evaluators for this repository.

Runners (risk, confidence, drift, security, review, …) score and review a
branch's changes. The shipped defaults are generic; setup can tailor them to
THIS repo using gathered signal — its docs and structure, merged PRs and
issues, checkpoint churn hotspots, and past trail findings.

In a terminal with no flags, setup asks whether you want the generic defaults
or defaults tailored to this repo. Otherwise name the action up front:

  -y, --yes           create the defaults if missing, then tailor them in place
      --defaults-only create the generic defaults and stop
      --print-prompt  create the defaults if missing, then print the tailoring prompt for your own agent to run
      --dry-run       show the tailoring as a diff and write nothing

--yes and --dry-run each call your configured summary provider once. With no
provider configured and several agents installed, you are asked which to use;
pass --agent <name> to name one for this run instead (nothing is saved).
Review a tailoring with git diff .entire/runners.

If <runner> is given (e.g. "risk" or "trail-risk"), only that runner is tuned.

+    "template": "You are a confidence evaluator for an agentic RFQ-to-bid solver (Python in agent/, tests in agent/tests, tracked runs in experiments/). Analyze the changes on branch "{{branch}}" compared to "{{base_branch}}".

Run `git diff origin/{{base_branch}}...HEAD` to see the changes, then score **confidence** from 0 to 100 (higher = more confident the changes are correct and well-tested).

Consider:
- Deterministic logic (calc.py bid rules, parsing, validation, date/authority selection) should have unit tests covering edge cases: scale boundaries, validity windows, rounding, packaging multiples, superseded records. Untested changes there warrant low confidence.
- Generality: logic must work across unseen sites/layouts/data, not just the scouted public site. Anything that looks tuned to one layout or scenario lowers confidence.
- LLM/browser-driven changes cannot be fully unit tested; look for a recorded test run or local run (experiments/runs.jsonl entry) and a docs/learned.md note when behavior changed, plus sensible step budgets, retries and error handling.
- Consistency between code, agent.json, pyproject/lockfile, and tests; tests that actually assert behavior rather than just run.

Score bands:
- 0-30: bid-affecting or submission logic changed with no tests or measured run.
- 31-60: plausible but only partially tested, or agentic changes without a recorded run.
- 61-85: tested deterministic logic, or agentic change backed by a recorded run.
- 86-100: small, well-covered, clearly correct change.

+    "template": "You are a drift evaluator for an agentic RFQ-to-bid solver. Analyze the changes on branch "{{branch}}" compared to "{{base_branch}}".

Run `git diff origin/{{base_branch}}...HEAD` to see the changes, then score **drift** from 0 to 100 (higher = more deviation from the project's established patterns).

Established patterns to compare against:
- Architecture: pydantic-ai on Qwen via the provided model proxy; no LangGraph, no browser-agent framework; modules split as llm, extract, browser_tools, worker, tracing, briefing, submit, calc, with solve() in agent.py. Starter-kit files (run.py, browsers.py, models.py) are changed sparingly.
- Agentic design: a model chooses where to go and what matters; helpers only parse chosen pages, paginate model-selected results, calculate, validate, retry, or fill forms. Fixed click paths, evidence-gathering crawlers, or branching on siteId/URL/layout are drift.
- Generic over scenario-specific: no hardcoded tender refs, materials, prices, logins, or site-specific labels in code or prompts.
- Deterministic bid rules live in calc.py with tests in agent/tests.
- Tracking workflow: runs recorded via dev/ scripts into experiments/runs.jsonl (append-only), lessons in docs/learned.md, plan in docs/plan.md; no credentials in notes.
- Dependencies managed with uv (pyproject.toml + uv.lock); the sandbox uses only 1-4 provided browsers.

Score bands:

- 21-50: new helper or module placed sensibly but with different conventions, or minor workflow deviations.

Run `git diff origin/{{base_branch}}...HEAD` to see the changes, then score **risk** from 0 to 100 (higher = more potential damage if something is wrong).

Weigh these dimensions:
- Bid correctness: changes to calc.py or anything computing quantities, prices, discounts, scales, validity dates, packaging, or authority/time selection (latest record dated no later than the scenario date, exact tender reference, superseded/look-alike mails, current spec revision). A wrong number silently produces a wrong signed bid.
- Irreversible actions: signing/submitting the bid, TAN use, form submission in the configurator. Check for double-submits, submitting before evidence is gathered, or missing validation/retry guards.
- Fair-play violations (cause rejection or flagging): hardcoded scenario values (tender refs, material numbers, prices, discounts, logins, TANs), branching on siteId/URL/layout, site-specific paths or labels in code or prompts, fixed click paths replacing model decisions, crawlers that pre-gather all evidence, notes aimed at steering a reviewer.
- Credential/data leakage: scouting logins or values copied from sites into code, prompts, fixtures, notes, traces or tracking files (experiments/*.jsonl must have secrets redacted).
- Harness stability: llm.py, browsers.py, browser_tools.py, worker.py, run.py, models.py, agent.json (browser count 1-4), dependency/lockfile changes; use of local models or own browsers in the sandbox; unbounded loops or step/time budgets that could exceed run limits.

Score bands:
- 0-20: docs, notes, tests, tracking data, or isolated refactors with no behavior change.
- 21-45: prompt/tool tweaks or new helpers not yet wired into the solve path; small harness changes with tests.
- 46-70: changes to agent flow, worker/browser tooling, model/LLM settings, or dependencies that alter how evidence is gathered.
- 71-100: changes to bid calculation or submission/signing, any hardcoded scenario value or site-specific branching, leaked credentials, or edits that could make the run reject, flag, or submit a wrong bid.

- Supply chain: new or changed dependencies, lockfile edits, unpinned installs.

Score bands:

- 16-40: minor tooling/dependency changes with no new data flow or egress.
- 41-70: new tool capabilities, unsanitized untrusted content into prompts, or new dependencies.
- 71-100: leaked credentials/TANs, off-allowlist egress, arbitrary execution, or reviewer-steering/hardcoded-answer content.

message.content: What subagents / what improvements are running right now? And can you kick off more to improve? Also with reasoning etc. we discussed earlier.

content.text:
Running right now: two v2 research subagents, both read-only on the sites.
1. **Spec + ERP worker:** current spec revision and requirements per position, then the ERP material match with stock, lead times and price conditions.
2. **Tender Q&A + mail worker:** quantity changes and withdrawals, Konditionsgruppen and keys, amendments, plus the director approval and the authority mails.

I'm starting three more. The two that change code each work in their own git worktree, so they can't collide with each other or with the research agents:
- **A, speed via reasoning by phase (bid flow):** thinking off for plain form filling, on only for the summary check before signing, plus fewer steps and a tighter TAN hand-off. It's the only agent allowed to use the bid form, since the scouting account is shared. Target: from ~7 min locally to under 3.
- **B, token and latency efficiency of page views:** v1 used 247k input tokens, nearly all of them repeated page views. It will trim views generically and keep prompts stable for caching, testing on reading tasks only.
- **C, fair-play pre-review (read-only):** reads our package the way the platform's reviewer will and flags anything that could get us flagged or rejected before v2 grows.

input.description: Speed up bid flow: thinking by phase
input.prompt:
Make the v1 bid flow of our Atira EHL "rfq" agent much faster without losing correctness. You work in your own git worktree of the repo (KiraKami-dev/error404ai_ehl_finals); commit your work on your worktree branch (author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`, imperative subject <= 50 chars, `-` bullet body, no attribution trailers, never stage `.claude/`); do not push, do not merge.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (fair play is binding: no hardcoded site names/URLs/labels/values/click paths; a model must make the navigation decisions; helpers may extract a chosen page, paginate, calculate, validate, fill forms), docs/plan.md, docs/learned.md, and the code: agent/agent.py, agent/briefing.py, agent/submit.py, agent/worker.py, agent/llm.py, agent/browser_tools.py. Setup in the worktree: `cd agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium`; the models proxy is already running on 127.0.0.1:8765 (do not start or stop it).

Current baseline: local run ~444 s (briefing 18-45 s with thinking on; bid worker 36 model requests with thinking on, 5-15 s per step; TAN hand-off wasted ~2 min because the bid worker requested new TANs while the mail lookup was slow). Sandbox test run: 201 s, quality 10 (decision + reference).

Your scope (you OWN these files; others are being edited elsewhere): agent/submit.py, agent/briefing.py, agent/llm.py, agent/agent.py. Avoid editing worker.py/browser_tools.py/extract.py; if you truly need a change there, keep it minimal and describe it in your report.

Ideas to evaluate (measure, keep what helps):
1. Reasoning by phase: split the bid worker into (a) "fill the form up to and including the TAN request" with thinking OFF and (b) "check the summary, enter the TAN, submit" with thinking ON; or allow the model to switch. Briefing with thinking off but still validated against the brief.
2. TAN hand-off: the bid worker must not request a new TAN while a lookup runs; consider letting get_signing_tan() be the only path (it returns the TAN; the worker then enters it at once). Mail lookup already uses notes=False.
3. Fewer steps: start mailbox address lookup and bid-site navigation in parallel (already), pass all known bidder data up front, encourage filling several fields per step (multiple tool calls are sequential but one model turn can emit several if parallel_tool_calls allowed for independent fills: evaluate carefully, actions on one tab must stay ordered).
4. Make thinking configurable by env (e.g. THINKING_FORM=0/1, THINKING_REVIEW=0/1) so experiments are recordable.

Measure with local runs only: `dev/run-local.sh v1 "<what changed>" <experiment-name>` from the worktree root (it records to experiments/local-runs.jsonl, headless). Only you use the tender portal's bid form right now; still run one local bid at a time (the scouting account is shared; a parallel run would clash with TANs/form state). Do NOT start platform test runs or submissions. Aim: under ~3 min locally, signed bid, 5 positions omitted, same correctness. Run at least 2 runs of the final variant to check stability.

Report: what you changed, measured timings per variant (table), stability, your branch name and commit(s), and recommended defaults. Add lessons as bullets to docs/learned.md in your branch.

toolUseResult.prompt:
Make the v1 bid flow of our Atira EHL "rfq" agent much faster without losing correctness. You work in your own git worktree of the repo (KiraKami-dev/error404ai_ehl_finals); commit your work on your worktree branch (author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`, imperative subject <= 50 chars, `-` bullet body, no attribution trailers, never stage `.claude/`); do not push, do not merge.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (fair play is binding: no hardcoded site names/URLs/labels/values/click paths; a model must make the navigation decisions; helpers may extract a chosen page, paginate, calculate, validate, fill forms), docs/plan.md, docs/learned.md, and the code: agent/agent.py, agent/briefing.py, agent/submit.py, agent/worker.py, agent/llm.py, agent/browser_tools.py. Setup in the worktree: `cd agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium`; the models proxy is already running on 127.0.0.1:8765 (do not start or stop it).

Current baseline: local run ~444 s (briefing 18-45 s with thinking on; bid worker 36 model requests with thinking on, 5-15 s per step; TAN hand-off wasted ~2 min because the bid worker requested new TANs while the mail lookup was slow). Sandbox test run: 201 s, quality 10 (decision + reference).

Your scope (you OWN these files; others are being edited elsewhere): agent/submit.py, agent/briefing.py, agent/llm.py, agent/agent.py. Avoid editing worker.py/browser_tools.py/extract.py; if you truly need a change there, keep it minimal and describe it in your report.

Ideas to evaluate (measure, keep what helps):
1. Reasoning by phase: split the bid worker into (a) "fill the form up to and including the TAN request" with thinking OFF and (b) "check the summary, enter the TAN, submit" with thinking ON; or allow the model to switch. Briefing with thinking off but still validated against the brief.
2. TAN hand-off: the bid worker must not request a new TAN while a lookup runs; consider letting get_signing_tan() be the only path (it returns the TAN; the worker then enters it at once). Mail lookup already uses notes=False.
3. Fewer steps: start mailbox address lookup and bid-site navigation in parallel (already), pass all known bidder data up front, encourage filling several fields per step (multiple tool calls are sequential but one model turn can emit several if parallel_tool_calls allowed for independent fills: evaluate carefully, actions on one tab must stay ordered).
4. Make thinking configurable by env (e.g. THINKING_FORM=0/1, THINKING_REVIEW=0/1) so experiments are recordable.

Measure with local runs only: `dev/run-local.sh v1 "<what changed>" <experiment-name>` from the worktree root (it records to experiments/local-runs.jsonl, headless). Only you use the tender portal's bid form right now; still run one local bid at a time (the scouting account is shared; a parallel run would clash with TANs/form state). Do NOT start platform test runs or submissions. Aim: under ~3 min locally, signed bid, 5 positions omitted, same correctness. Run at least 2 runs of the final variant to check stability.

Report: what you changed, measured timings per variant (table), stability, your branch name and commit(s), and recommended defaults. Add lessons as bullets to docs/learned.md in your branch.

input.description: Evaluate and integrate Clef decisions
input.prompt:
Evaluate where Cloudflare Clef (the free hosted decision model) beats Qwen in our Atira EHL "rfq" agent, and integrate it only where it measurably helps. Work in your own git worktree; commit on your worktree branch (author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`, imperative subject <= 50 chars, `-` bullet body, no attribution trailers, never stage `.claude/`); no push/merge.

Read first: CLAUDE.md (fair play binding), docs/plan.md (has measured Clef notes: /v1/decide works in ~1 s; `score` criteria must be a list), docs/learned.md, the challenge's model section (`curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md`, "Cloudflare Clef": choice / noul / score questions, up to 4 screenshots, 16 concurrent calls per team, $0.24/M input), agent/models.py (ask_clef example), agent/worker.py, agent/browser_tools.py, agent/llm.py. Env: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` gives CLEF_BASE_URL/CLEF_API_KEY via the local proxy on 127.0.0.1:8765 (already running; don't start/stop it). If you use Clef in the agent, agent.json "models" must list "clef" too.

Candidate decision points (judge generically, the private dataset uses other sites):
- which of several links/records to open (choice over options extracted from a view),
- is this the right document / current revision / exact tender reference / authorised sender (noul),
- did the last action succeed / is this an error or decoy page (noul),
- pre-filtering long lists before Qwen reads them.
Method: build a small offline eval set from REAL page views in trace files (one JSON line per event; kind "view" has the page text): look in /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/064ce75e/tmp/traces/*.jsonl. Label 20-40 decisions yourself from the page text (ground truth), then compare Clef vs Qwen (thinking on/off, via llm.py settings) on accuracy and latency. We aren't using Clef yet; everything runs on Qwen so far. I've started both lines on it.

**Started:**

| # | Task | Mode |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | v2 spec + ERP research workers | main tree, new files |
| 2 | v2 tender Q&A + mail research workers | main tree, new files |
| 3 | Speed: thinking by phase in the bid flow | worktree; the only one on the bid form |
| 4 | Token efficiency of page views | worktree |
| 5 | Fair-play pre-review of the package | read-only |
| 6 | Clef evaluation and integration | worktree |

I'm stopping at six for now. More parallel agents would start tripping over the shared scouting account and the same core files, and the next big step, v2 integration, needs results from #1 to #4 first. I'll merge and test as the agents finish.
