input.description: Find and fix the event-loop hang
input.prompt:
Find and fix a hard hang in our Atira EHL "rfq" agent. Work in your own git worktree (based on main); commit on your branch (author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`, imperative subject <= 50 chars, blank line, `-` bullets; keep the `Entire-Checkpoint:` line; no Co-Authored-By; never stage `.claude/`); no push/merge. ~40 minutes; commit early. Avoid editing agent/orchestrator.py, research*.py (another agent edits them); keep changes in browser_tools.py, extract.py, worker.py, agent.py, tracing.py, llm.py as small as possible.

Evidence: sandbox test run run_f93eb9b4b292ae71 (main at 0103702) logged normally until 362 s (mail tabs doing human checks, an ERP settle timeout at 351 s), then NOTHING for 20+ minutes: no model calls, no actions, no errors, and the agent's own deadlines (asyncio.wait_for in run_worker, settle capped at 45 s, research deadline) never fired, so the run never signed. That points to the asyncio event loop being blocked by synchronous work or a deadlock. Log: /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/064ce75e/tmp/rf93.log (the run's stdout; `[model]` lines are model calls).

Suspects to check (read the code): CPU-heavy pure-Python work on large text in the loop: the view diffing in extract.py/browser_tools.py (difflib.SequenceMatcher is quadratic on large inputs), the grounding check unseen_values()/ungrounded() over session.seen (which grows with every view), regexes with catastrophic backtracking, JSON of huge traces; awaits without timeouts that can't be cancelled cleanly (page.evaluate in extract.observe on a frozen page, frame.evaluate per frame, locator.count/inner_text without timeout); asyncio.Lock re-entrance/deadlocks (SiteSession.lock is not re-entrant: e.g. a path that takes session.lock and then calls something that takes it again, Mailbox lock + session lock ordering); sync file I/O in tracing on big views.

Do:
1. An event-loop watchdog (agent.py or a small module): a daemon thread checks a heartbeat the loop updates every second; if stale > 20 s, dump all thread stacks once (faulthandler.dump_traceback to stdout, so it lands in the run log) and log a line; repeat at most every 60 s. This makes the next occurrence diagnosable.
2. Make likely blockers safe: cap/replace the diff (e.g. diff only when both texts are < ~20k chars, use a linear line-set diff, or run CPU-heavy steps via asyncio.to_thread with a timeout); make the grounding check scale (e.g. a set of normalised tokens built incrementally instead of searching a growing string); put timeouts on every page/frame evaluate and locator call in extract/browser_tools; check lock usage for re-entrance and fix.
3. Reproduce what you can locally: unit tests with large synthetic pages (e.g. 200k-char views) showing look()/diff/grounding stay fast (< 1 s), a test that a hung page.evaluate is cut by its timeout (e.g. a page with an infinite JS loop: page.evaluate on it hangs), and a lock re-entrance test if you find one.
4. Tests pass (`cd agent && uv sync -q && uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests`). Then run 1 sandbox test run of your branch with `dev/test-run.sh v2 "<note>" hang-fix` from your worktree root (max 1 in flight).
Report: the most likely cause (with evidence), fixes, test results, branch and commits.

<summary>Agent "Find and fix the event-loop hang" finished</summary>
<note>This agent stopped with background work of its own still running. It may resume on its own when that work completes or reports, and the same task-id notifies again if it does; the result below may be interim.</note>
<result>I couldn't pin down the exact cause of the hang from the log. The fixes for every likely blocker are committed, along with a watchdog that will dump stacks if it happens again. The sandbox run of the branch did not hang, but it also failed (score 0) for a different reason, described below.

**Most likely cause.** "Nothing at all for 20+ min, and no deadline ever fired" fits a blocked event loop better than a hung await. The log shows nothing that blocks for that long, so the candidates are:
- **Frozen page plus unbounded calls.** I reproduced this locally: on a tab running an endless JS loop, `page.evaluate`, `frame.evaluate`, `page.title()` and `locator.count()` hang forever with no timeout. Other tabs keep working, and `asyncio.wait_for` does cut these calls. `observe()`, `look()`, `locate()`, `_human_check` and `_collect_closed` had no bound. `look()` is also called outside any `wait_for` in many places, including the first view in `run_worker`. The two `Locator.evaluate: Timeout 30000ms exceeded` errors on mail tabs, and the 45 s settle timeout on the ERP tab, show pages becoming unresponsive just before the silence. On its own this explains a stuck worker, not the missed deadlines.
- **Quadratic regex in the grounding check.** `unseen_values()` used `[\w/.:,+-]*\d[\w/.:,+-]*`, which is quadratic on any long run of those characters with no digit. Measured: 20k characters take 1.1 s, so 200k would take about 110 s and 1M about 45 min, all on the loop. It only runs on model output and notes, and the mail workers run with `grounded=False`, so it probably isn't what hung at 362 s.
- **Ruled out:**
  - The diff in `changes()` is only run on views of 14k characters or less, and stays around 10 ms on a worst-case table.
  - I found no `SiteSession.lock` re-entrance. Mailbox lock then session lock is always taken in that order, never reversed.
  - Nothing swallows `CancelledError`.
- **Infra possibility.** If the sandbox stopped reading stdout, `print(flush=True)` would block the whole loop and give exactly this picture. I can't verify that from our side.

**Fixes (commit `630849a`):**
- **Watchdog:** new `agent/loopwatch.py`, started in `agent.solve()`.
  - A daemon thread watches a 1 s heartbeat. If the loop is stale for more than 20 s, it prints a `[watchdog]` line and dumps every thread's stack to stdout with `faulthandler`, at most once a minute.
  - If the loop still runs but no trace event has appeared for 300 s, it dumps all asyncio task stacks. That catches the deadlock case too.
  - `tracing.py` now records the time of the latest event (two lines).
- **`extract.py`:** the page walk is capped at 20 s. Per-frame evaluates, `locate()`'s `count()` and `select_options` are capped at 5 to 20 s. `changes()` returns None (send the whole view) when the two views together exceed 40k characters.
- **`browser_tools.py`:**
  - The human-check and popup-collect frame evaluates have timeouts, and so does `page.title()`.
  - `look()` now returns "(the page does not respond …)" instead of hanging when its retry also fails.
  - `unseen_values()` uses a linear regex that gives the same results. It also searches `seen` directly instead of rebuilding a whitespace-normalised copy on every call; values contain no whitespace, so the result is the same.

**Tests.** The new `agent/tests/test_hang.py` checks that:
- a 250k-character diff and the grounding check (200k-character token against about 2 MB of history) each finish in under 1 s;
- a frozen page is cut off and `look()` returns a note, while another tab still works;
- the Python side of `look()` on a 100k+ character page takes under 1 s;
- the watchdog dumps on a blocked loop and on a silent run.

The full suite passes: 142 tests.

**Sandbox run `run_a27e8c91f74fdb41`:** failed with score 0.
- tender-portal, which is the bid site, never opened (repeated 45 s settle timeouts), so research had nothing to build on.
- There was no hang and no watchdog dump: the research deadline fired at 630 s as designed.
- The run then crashed with `IndexError` in `SiteSession.page` (`open_pages[-1]` on an empty list), reached from `look()` when `submit_bid()` started the bid worker on a session with no tab.
- That crash is an existing bug, and the fix belongs in `submit.py` or `agent.py`, which I left alone. Someone should make `submit_bid` reopen the bid site, or exit cleanly, when its session has no tab.
- The website's log stream timed out twice while I followed the run; I recorded the result with `dev/track.py --force`. `experiments/runs.jsonl` now has two lines for this run, an early "running" one and the final "failed" one.

**Branch:** `worktree-agent-a6e9ece93fe436042`, with commits `630849a` (the fixes) and `1374502` (the run record). The `Entire-Checkpoint` line is kept and there is no session trailer. Nothing was pushed or merged.</result>

input.prompt:
Read-only analysis for our Atira EHL "rfq" agent: why do v2 sandbox runs sometimes reach 100 and sometimes not? Do not edit code, do not start runs, do not commit. Repo: /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/EHL_Finale/error404ai_ehl_finals (read CLAUDE.md, docs/learned.md, experiments/runs.jsonl).

Collect the logs of every v2 sandbox run (test runs and the promoted submission) since 19:20 UTC: list them with `atira status </dev/null` (always </dev/null; use timeouts >= 150 s, the platform is slow) and `python3 dev/track.py report` / experiments/runs.jsonl; fetch each log with `atira logs <run_id> </dev/null > /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/064ce75e/tmp/logs/<run_id>.log` (some already exist in /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/064ce75e/tmp/*.log) and scores with `atira status <run_id> --json </dev/null`. Known runs include run_06a3e95a007b9c33 (100), run_715aa132bf4a5c38 (100), run_df14f82a49438b67 (10), run_f910fa6f7395082f (no bid), run_817c4ff00600912d (10), run_9371dffa1ac79744 (0), run_a27e8c91f74fdb41 (0), run_6a01d429127aebb6 (hung, cancelled), run_f93eb9b4b292ae71 (hung, cancelled), plus any newer ones.
The log lines are our trace: `[  t s] worker kind key=value ...` (kinds: start, done, stopped, problem, helper, helper_error, action, spec_done, tender_facts, mail_kind, calc, verify, orchestrator, summary_check, last_chance, ...) and `[model] status seconds bytes` lines per model call.

Produce (under 700 words, plus one table):
1. Per run: score breakdown (points per field), timeline per phase (briefing, session starts, planner, tender, spec, ERP, mail per kind, verify, calc, form, signing) with start/end seconds, and the first failure that cost points.
2. Model-call stats per run: count, median/p90/max latency, calls > 45 s, retries/timeouts; and site slowness signals (settle timeouts, start_failed, error pages).
3. A failure taxonomy ranked by points lost x frequency, and a critical-path analysis: what the successful 100 runs did differently (timings, which kinds/workers finished when).
4. Concrete recommendations with numbers: per-phase budgets/deadlines that would have let the failing runs finish, where redundancy/parallelism pays most, which step limits are too low/high.
Write the full analysis also to /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/064ce75e/tmp/v2_analysis.md.
